updates.how: To cope with the specific power unit cooling challenges in Mexico, the cooling louvres have been extended forwards and reshaped.
To recover cooling mass flow through the radiators, the exit area has been increased by extending the area of the existing louvres and optional louvres further outboard.

updates.how: Attached to existing sidepod geometry to improve the flow characteristics below the inlet to the radiator duct gaining local load whilst maintaining stability.

updates.how: engine cooling capacity, at the expense of car efficiency
The main cooling exit at the rear of the bodywork has been enlarged, to increase the available engine cooling to suit the high demands of this circuit.
To further extend the cooling range in extreme conditions, an additional forward louvre panel is available which allows for increased airflow through the radiators.
The revised rear brake duct deflector geometry represents a local rear corner aerodynamic load increase, improving the overall aerodynamic performance of the car.
For Mexico, the tailpipe vane configuration has been trimmed to suit the track’s unique ambient and aerodynamic requirements.
